title: FIDE rankings: September 2025
content: The September 2025 FIDE rankings show a significant rise for German Grandmaster Vincent Keymer, who gained 21 points at the Chennai tournament to reach an Elo rating of 2751 and climb from 21st to 10th place in the world.  Keymer’s jump is the largest in the 2700+ range, with only Kirill Alexeenko (+22) and Dmitry Andreikin (+15) matching or approaching it.  The top of the rankings remains dominated by Magnus Carlsen, Hikaru Nakamura and Fabiano Caruana, followed by Indian players Praggnanandhaa, Arjun Erigaisi and world champion Gukesh.  In the women’s list, Zhu Jiner moved into fourth place with an 11‑point gain, overtaking Tan Zhongyi who fell from fourth to seventh after losing eight points.  15‑year‑old Lu Miaoyi improved to 23rd place with a 10‑point gain after winning the Dortmund Women’s Tournament.  Other notable moves include Nino Batsiashvili’s 28‑point jump to 18th, Polina Shuvalova’s 12 points to 12th, and Tatev Abrahamyan’s 64‑point surge to 18th.  The junior section still highlights Praggnanandhaa, Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov as the only players over 2700, while the Turkish pair Ediz Gürel and Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus swapped positions.  The biggest individual gain was Marija Kuznecova’s 72 points, taking her to 33rd place.  Keymer’s rise marks the first time since Robert Hübner that a German has entered the world’s top ten, and it reflects a broader increase in the Elo levels of the elite.

title: Gukesh Dommaraju drops out of FIDE top 10; Divya Deshmukh rises to No. 11 in women's rankings
content: India's chess prodigy Gukesh Dommaraju, the reigning world champion and youngest in history to hold the title, has dropped out of the FIDE top 10 in the October 2025 world rankings. After losing three games and drawing four over 11 rounds at the FIDE Grand Swiss tournament in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, where he placed 41st out of 116 players, his rating fell by 15 points to 2752, down from 2767 in September and 43 points from his peak of 2794 in October 2024. Meanwhile, Indian player Divya Deshmukh has risen to No. 11 in the women's FIDE rankings following a strong performance over the past month.

title: D Gukesh slips out of top ten in official FIDE chess rankings, Arjun Erigaisi India No. 1
content: D Gukesh has slipped to 11th in the official FIDE classical chess rankings, with a rating of 2752, after losing 15 rating points from 2767 in September to 2752 in October, marking a 43-point decline from his October 2024 rating of 2794. Magnus Carlsen remains World No. 1 with a rating of 2839, followed by Hikaru Nakamura (2816, +9), Fabiano Caruana (2789), Arjun Erigaisi (2773, World No. 4), R Praggnanandhaa (2771, No. 5), Alireza Firouzja (2762, No. 6), Anish Giri (2759, No. 7), Wesley So (2756, No. 8), Vincent Keymer (2755, No. 9), and Wei Yi (2754, No. 10). Viswanathan Anand commented on Gukesh's recent form, stating he is 'having a bumpy time' and attributing the dip to a combination of factors, including the pressure of being world champion and the high competitiveness of the current chess scene. Anand expressed optimism, noting Gukesh's resilience in accepting new challenges, including participation in the World Cup, and emphasized that he has 'a whole year to get ready' to recover. Anand also clarified that Gukesh's struggles are not due to 'tactical blips' but rather a period of adjustment to his new role.

title: El monarca Gukesh baja del 6 al 11 en FIDE
content: Indian chess prodigy Gukesh Dommaraju, 19, dropped from 6th to 11th place in the FIDE October 2025 rating list following a poor performance at the Samarcanda Grand Swiss, where he suffered three consecutive losses to Abhimanyu Mishra (USA), Nilokás Theodorou (Greece), and Ediz Gurel (Turkey, age 16). His result of (+2, =4, -3) placed him 41st in the tournament, causing him to fall out of the top 10. His Elo rating decreased to 2,752. Meanwhile, American grandmaster Hans Moke Niemann rose to 12th place with 2,738 points after finishing 7th in Samarcanda. The top 10 includes Magnus Carlsen (Norway, 2,839), Hikaru Nakamura (USA, 2,816), Fabiano Caruana (USA, 2,789), and others. The list features 30 players born in the 21st century, including 14-year-old prodigies Abhimanyu Mishra (2,652) and Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus (2,651), both of whom earned their GM titles at exceptionally young ages. The FIDE ratings reflect the mathematical precision of the Elo system, which measures player strength without emotional bias. In the Grand Chess Tour final in São Paulo, Maxime Vachier-Lagrave and Fabiano Caruana drew their classical game and later tied in rapid and blitz, resulting in a shared final. Praggnanandhaa and Levon Aronian also drew their third-place playoff.

title: FIDE World Cup 2025 D Gukesh Top Seed, Followed By Arjun Erigaisi & R Praggnanandhaa
content: The FIDE World Cup 2025 will begin on October 30 in Goa, India, with reigning world champion D Gukesh as the top seed, followed by compatriots Arjun Erigaisi and R Praggnanandhaa. Anish Giri is the fourth seed, and the top three finishers will earn direct qualification spots for the 2026 Candidates Tournament. The tournament features 206 players from around the world and offers a prize pool of USD 2 million. The format is an eight-round knockout, with the top 50 seeds advancing automatically to the second round. Each round spans three days, consisting of two classical games (90 minutes for the first 40 moves, followed by 30 minutes with a 30-second increment per move), and rapid tie-breaks if needed. The schedule runs from October 30 to November 27, with rounds 1–3 from November 1–9, a rest day on November 10, rounds 4–6 from November 11–19, another rest day on November 20, and the final two rounds from November 21–26. USA’s Wesley So is fifth seed, followed by Vincent Keymer, Wei Yi, Nodirbek Abdusattorov, Shakhriyar Mamedyarov, and Hans Niemann. The men’s World Cup is separate from the women’s tournament, which was held in July and won by Divya Deshmukh, who earned the grandmaster title and a 2026 Women’s Candidates spot.

title: FIDE Rankings, September 2025: Praggnanandhaa touches career-high rating; Carlsen continues on top
content: Indian grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa’s classical rating rose to a career‑high 2785 in the September 2025 FIDE ranking update, a gain helped by his second‑place finish at the Sinquefield Cup 2025 that added six rating points in August.  Praggnanandhaa is now the highest‑ranked Indian player in classical chess, occupying fourth place.  Reigning world champion D Gukesh is ranked sixth, while Arjun Erigaisi is also fourth.  Five‑time world champion Magnus Carlsen remains at the top of the world rankings, with American grandmasters Hikaru Nakamura and Fabiano Caruana following at second and third respectively.  Germany’s Vincent Keymer entered the top ten for the first time after a dominant win at the Chennai Grand Masters 2025, gaining 21 rating points and moving up 11 places.  American grandmaster Wesley So jumped to seventh after his second title win at the Sinquefield Cup.  In women’s classical chess, China’s Hou Yifan continues to hold the top spot, and Koneru Humpy is the highest‑ranked Indian woman at sixth.

title: FIDE rankings: D Gukesh no longer in top 10, Divya Deshmukh continues to soar
content: According to the FIDE October 2025 ratings list released on October 5, 2025, Gukesh Dommaraju, the reigning world chess champion, is no longer in the top 10 players, dropping to a rating of 2752 after losing 15 points in the eleven-round FIDE Grand Swiss in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, where he finished 41st out of 116 players. This follows a 43-point decline from his October 2024 rating of 2794. Divya Deshmukh, ranked 11th with a rating of 2498, achieved significant success by winning the Women's World Cup, qualifying for the Women's Candidates tournament, and defeating two grandmasters while drawing with Gukesh in the open section of the Grand Swiss. Vaishali R. defended her Women's Grand Swiss title and gained 21 rating points, reaching her highest-ever ranking of 15th. Arjun Erigaisi, ranked fourth globally with 2773 points, remains India's highest-ranked player, followed by Praggnanandhaa at fifth with 2771, though Praggnanandhaa lost 14 rating points during the Grand Swiss. Magnus Carlsen leads the rankings with 2839 points, the only player above 2800, followed by Hikaru Nakamura. Koneru Humpy remains India's top female player at world no. 6.

title: Chess | D Gukesh out of top 10 in latest FIDE rankings; Arjun Erigaisi surpasses R Praggnanandhaa to become India No. 1 | Chess News - The Times of India
content: In September 2025, Indian chess achieved a historic milestone as Arjun Erigaisi rose to world number four in the FIDE rankings, while Nihal Sarin joined the elite 2700 Elo club. Vaishali Rameshbabu secured a spot in the Women's Candidates Tournament, and Divya Deshmukh delivered strong performances. Junior players Pranav Venkatesh, Abhimanyu Mishra, and Ashwath Kaushik also recorded significant rating increases, highlighting India's growing prominence as a global chess powerhouse. Additionally, D Gukesh fell out of the top 10 in the latest FIDE rankings, and Arjun Erigaisi surpassed R Praggnanandhaa to become India's top-ranked player.

title: Praggnanandhaa has historic world No. 3 FIDE ranking spot up for grabs after stunning world champion Gukesh
content: Indian Grandmaster Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa has secured the world No. 3 spot in the live FIDE ranking for the first time after a stunning win over world champion D Gukesh at the Sinquefield Cup 2025. Praggnanandhaa overtook Fabiano Caruana in the live rating and now faces his closest competitor Caruana in the second round. Praggnanandhaa's highest FIDE ranking is No. 4, which he achieved in July 2025. He has an Elo rating of 2784 currently in live standings, his personal best. Praggnanandhaa said, 'This is my first classical win in like three years and the previous one I got was also lucky because he was completely winning throughout.' He also reflected on Gukesh's game, saying, 'It was a smooth game. It was surprising from him because he was off at the start, like he spent so much time at a theoretical position and this endgame is just unpleasant for him.'

title: FIDE ratings - October 2025
content: According to the FIDE ratings released on October 1, 2025, Magnus Carlsen remains the world's top-ranked player in classical, blitz, and rapid chess, despite playing fewer classical games. Wesley So has returned to the world's top ten after winning the Sinquefield Cup, ranking 8th with a rating of 2756, one point ahead of Vincent Keymer (2755), who is ranked 9th. Matthias Blübaum rose to 41st globally with 2687 points following his performance at the FIDE Grand Swiss in Samarkand. Chinese women continue to dominate the women's rankings: Hou Yifan, the only woman with a rating above 2600, is ranked number one, followed by three other Chinese players. Of the top ten women, five are from China, and Aleksandra Goryachkina is the highest-rated non-Chinese woman. Among juniors (under 20), Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu is ranked 5th globally and 1st in the junior rankings, while reigning world champion Gukesh Dommaraju, who lost some Elo points at the Samarkand Grand Swiss, is 2nd in the junior rankings. India leads in junior women's rankings, with Divya Deshmukh ranked 1st globally at 2498, 54 points ahead of China’s Song Yuxin, who is 2nd among girls born in 2005 or later.
